reader_notes: Independent reading from the note text (tools/inventions/dump.ts, bars 1-62; beats are eighths, so 1:1.5 is the off-beat sixteenth). No published analysis consulted. x = the bass's rising scale with turn, 1:1-4:2 (E3 F# G# | A B C# | D# E D# C# B | E4 E3). y = the right hand's syncopated chromatic descent with its ornamental tail, 1:1.5-4:3.75 (E5 D# D | C# B A | G# F# G#-A | G# B-A B G#-F# G# E-D#), entering half an eighth after x. The tail figure (a note, its upper neighbour pair, the note again: G# B A B ...) is called 'the turn figure'. The note text carries no repeat signs; the division at bar 20 is clear from the music (cadence in B, codetta, restart), but the presence of repeats is not checked here.

notes: Two halves: 1-20 (E to B) and 21-62 (B, g#, then E). The second half restates the first half's material in the tonic after a move away: alpha at 43-50, beta down a fifth at 51-59, the codetta at 60-62. That is the sonata shape of the protocol; the protocol's definition also asks for repeat signs, which the note text does not record (unsure only on that point; without them the form is rounded bipartite). About 42 of 62 bars are paradigm members (alpha 24, beta 18). Every member of alpha is exact apart from the bridging bars 46 and 50. Each restatement in a new key begins with the exchanged form (bars 21, 43), whereas the opening began with the original: the second half reverses the order of the pair.
